speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, and tell me exactly when it first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash appear to be blanching (turning white) when you press on it, and has it spread to her palms and soles? I also need to know if she has had any recent contact with someone who had a similar illness or visited a daycare recently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the facial rash spread to her trunk and limbs, and does it look like sunburn with a "slapped cheek" appearance? I also need to know if she has any swollen lymph nodes or joint pain.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash on her trunk and extremities have a lacy or reticular pattern? I also need to know if she has experienced any joint pain or swelling.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any respiratory distress, joint pains, or changes in bowel or urinary habits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the classic presentation of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities, along with the mild prodrome of fever and rhinorrhea, this is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
